text:
ConocoPhillips dropped 4.7% today after climbing nearly $4 over the previous trading day. The sharp reversal came despite oil prices remaining elevated—U.S. crude at $103/barrel and global crude at $123/barrel—suggesting the stock may have gotten ahead of itself on Friday's geopolitical premium. The timing matters: news of U.S. strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island and signals of potential diplomacy pushed the stock up sharply, but the market appears to have pulled back as it digests whether elevated oil will actually persist or if a negotiated settlement could defuse tensions and ease prices.

Rival oil majors like BP and Saudi Aramco are posting outsized profits as refining margins widen—the gap between crude costs and finished fuel prices—which should theoretically support ConocoPhillips' earnings. The sell-off despite healthy refining conditions and geopolitical risk premiums in crude prices suggests investors may be rotating out of energy stocks ahead of the midterm elections, or pricing in skepticism that today's oil spike will hold if diplomatic talks gain real traction.
